Guard (Top).label: Break posture and open closed guard to begin passing
Guard (Top).note: White belt advancement goal from inside closed guard: stay balanced, break posture, open the guard, and transition into a passing phase without getting swept.

ReactiveResponses.label: Off-balance and sweep as you try to open
ReactiveResponses.note: Best defense: uses your posture break or overcommitment to reverse the position and put you on bottom.

ReactiveResponses.label: Clamp closed guard and stall the opening attempt
ReactiveResponses.note: Safe defense: prevents immediate opening or passing but does not improve position. The exchange stays in closed guard.

ReactiveResponses.label: Open guard but lose control as you do
ReactiveResponses.note: Poor defense: opens the guard without maintaining frames or control, allowing you to stabilize in open guard top and start passing.

neutral.label: Grip and pull closed guard
neutral.note: A deliberate guard pull that resolves standing neutral into a known position. Prioritizes control and predictability over takedown risk.

ReactiveResponses.label: Posture up and immediately open + pass
ReactiveResponses.note: Best-case reaction: denies the guard pull from becoming stable offense and converts it into top control by quickly breaking the closed guard and passing.

ReactiveResponses.label: Accept guard but maintain posture and base
ReactiveResponses.note: Safe defense: avoids being broken down or swept, but does not improve position. Results in a stable closed-guard stalemate.

ReactiveResponses.label: Let posture get broken and give up control
ReactiveResponses.note: Poor defense: allows the guard pull to succeed cleanly with strong bottom control and initiative.

Guard (Bottom).label: Break posture and off-balance to sweep
Guard (Bottom).note: Primary white belt advancement from closed guard bottom. Focuses on breaking posture and creating imbalance to come up on top rather than forcing submissions.

ReactiveResponses.label: Opponent loses balance and gets swept
ReactiveResponses.note: Best-case outcome: posture is broken, balance is compromised, and the user completes a sweep into top control.

ReactiveResponses.label: Opponent regains posture and stabilizes
ReactiveResponses.note: Opponent defends correctly, regaining posture and base. Guard remains closed with no positional change.

ReactiveResponses.label: Posture break attempt fails and guard is passed
ReactiveResponses.note: Poor timing or control allows the opponent to open the guard and immediately pass to side control.
